comparator.name: Bachelor Electrical Engineering
comparator.sourceNotes: The official after-revision EE/AT curriculum for 2026–2027, latest version 2 July 2026, was freshly retrieved and inspected on 8 October 2026. Only common and EE rows are included; AT-only requirements and optional examples are not stacked into Electrical Engineering. Core 125 includes 5XEC0 Final Bachelor Project 10; ITEC Ethics 0LVX30 and Society 0LVX40 total 10; genuine free space is 45. Year one is core 60; year two core 40 + ITEC 5 + electives 15; year three core 25 including project + ITEC 5 + electives 30. All 27 positions total 180. Programming and Engineering Challenge 5EWC0 spans two quarters and is counted once at 10. This replaces the older 120/15/45 aggregates and unsupported compulsory-semiconductor claim. Semiconductor Technology 5XPG0 and optional medical/automotive examples are not universal core. Free electives remain generic under university approval, non-overlap and applicable level rules. The current table establishes required membership and credits; its project quarter/timeslot notation does not justify a guaranteed future timetable or individual admission. The prospectus was not freshly accessible; its historical audit evidence is identified separately. No new UCR judgment is made.

alternatives.label: Signals, control & intelligent connected systems
alternatives.concept: Combine mathematical system models with programming, algorithms, signal/image analysis, machine learning, robotics, networks, data management and product design for sensing, control and connected devices. This is a computational systems response, not electrical or electronic engineering equivalence.
alternatives.labelReason: The schedule contains a cumulative mathematical/computational sequence, linear systems, image-based sensing, robotics, networks and product design; the label avoids claiming circuits, electronics or embedded hardware.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Programming precedes algorithms, networks, planning and reinforcement learning; Mathematical Methods precedes dependent mathematics, robotics and neural networks. Numerical Methods and Linear Systems occur in the sole available fourth semester, while Advanced Calculus follows when next offered.

alternatives.label: Sustainable energy, system modelling & intelligent infrastructure
alternatives.concept: Retain mathematical modelling, data, perception, robotics and intelligent decisions while adding lifecycle assessment, renewable-energy design, climate context and resource recovery for sustainable energy and infrastructure questions.
alternatives.labelReason: Five sustainability courses create a cumulative lifecycle, energy and resource strand alongside quantitative intelligent-system methods; the label does not imply grid engineering, power electronics or electric machines.
progression: All exact Fall 2026-start availability and recorded formal prerequisites pass. Sustainability Essentials I precedes II, which precedes Renewable System Design and resource recovery. Programming and Mathematical Methods precede their dependent advanced courses. Advanced Calculus follows Numerical Methods and Linear Systems because its next exact offering is the final spring.
alternatives.distinctness: Five courses / 37.5 EC differ in each direction. Logic, databases, networks, advanced algorithms and AI ethics are replaced by two sustainability foundations, climate change, renewable-system design and resource recovery.

selection.assessment: Two related-fields responses pass the academic, schedule and 30-EC distinctness gates. The first owns the signals, sensing, control, connected-device and hardware/software interests through actual computational content. The second is independently supported by energy, sustainability and infrastructure interests. A circuits/semiconductors/electromagnetics direction cannot supply circuit analysis, analogue or digital electronics, semiconductor devices, fields/waves, instrumentation, microcontrollers, integrated circuits or hardware laboratories. Mathematical systems, general networks and renewable-system assessment cannot be relabelled as that formation. No third programme is manufactured.

They do not reproduce the target's circuits, analogue/digital electronics, electromagnetics, photonics, semiconductors, computer architecture, electric machines, power systems, instrumentation, hardware laboratories or electrical-engineering capstone.
